title: Invertibility of normalized finite-projective degreewise evaluation
statement: For a commutative ring A and cochain complexes P,Q on the one-object bottom-topology ringed site [def-pc-perfect-rhom-base-change-map], assume P is zero outside some finite interval and every evaluated P^p is finite projective. For each integer n, every morphism Tot(Hom(P,A[0]) tensor Q)^n to Hom(P,Q)^n satisfying the signed evaluation normalization [lem-pc-perfect-ring-hom-tensor-degree-condition] is an isomorphism. No bound on Q is required.

source.place: Tag 0A6A, lemma-base-change-RHom, clause (1), expanded chain-level evaluation; Tag 0ATK, lemma-base-change-evaluation-map, clause (1)

proof.text:
evaluation at the unique object identifies sheaves on the bottom-topology
one-object site with A-modules, identifies sheafification with the identity, and
reflects isomorphisms. Project the dual degree r to Hom(P^(-r),A[0]^0), then identify
A[0]^0 with A. The chosen product property is exposed by [lem-sc-hom-complex-projections]. The covariant internal-Hom functor preserves zero morphisms, so Mathlib Functor.map_isZero makes all other product factors zero. Thus this projection is invertible.
For each r+s=n, the diagonal block in the normalization is therefore the map
from the dual of P^(-r) tensor Q^s to Hom(P^(-r),Q^s), multiplied by (-1)^(r*s).
The first map is invertible by Mathlib dualTensorHomEquiv for the finite projective
module P^(-r); the scalar is a unit, since its square is one. The normalization
identifies this block on pure tensors, which generate the module tensor; all other
blocks vanish by its first clause. The bound on P restricts the nonzero Hom factors
to a finite interval, and also restricts the nonzero dual factors to its negative.
Index the tensor inclusions by r, with s=n-r, and index the Hom projections by p=-r. Let d_r denote the diagonal block. The finite sum over r in [-b,-a] of the Hom projection followed by d_r inverse and the tensor inclusion is a two-sided inverse. Check the first equation against the jointly epimorphic tensor inclusions and the second against the jointly monomorphic product projections. Outside the interval the Hom factor is zero by Functor.map_isZero for the contravariant internal-Hom functor, using PresheafOfModules.homObjMap_zero_left, and the diagonal isomorphism makes the corresponding tensor factor zero as well. Empty
support yields zero objects and the same inverse equations. No bound on Q is used,
and rank-zero modules and the zero ring are covered by the same argument.
